Vignette:
Kofi's eyes had always been drawn to design - the clean lines, the intuitive interfaces. As a UX designer at a startup in Brooklyn, he took pride in crafting experiences that felt seamless and safe for users. But his own life had become a jarring contrast. For months, Kofi had been looking over his shoulder, on edge every time his phone buzzed or a stranger passed him on the street. It started with the stalking - weeks of escalating messages and gifts from someone he'd met at a networking event. At first, it seemed like a harmless crush, but soon the tone shifted to menacing and possessive. Kofi changed his number, blocked her on social media, but somehow she always found ways to reach him. He began to feel like he was walking around with a target on his back. The memories of that time still felt jagged - the way she'd show up at his favorite coffee shop, or leave flowers outside his apartment door. Kofi had tried to brush it off as an annoyance, but deep down, he knew he wasn't being paranoid - this was someone who would stop at nothing to get close to him. As the stalking continued, Kofi's worldview began to warp. He became convinced that the world was a treacherous place, full of predators waiting for the perfect moment to strike. Every news story about violence or harassment felt like confirmation of his worst fears - I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next. His friends and family would try to reassure him, but Kofi just couldn't shake the feeling that he was walking on thin ice. One particular incident still haunted him - a night when she'd shown up outside his apartment building, pounding on the door until he'd called the police. The officers had taken her away, but not before she'd spat at him through the window, "You think you can hide from me?" Kofi's mind would replay that moment over and over, convinced that if only he'd done something differently - been more polite to her initially, or blocked her number sooner - none of this would have happened. The event had become a personal failing in his eyes. As the months dragged on, Kofi found himself withdrawing from social events, avoiding coffee shops and public spaces where she might find him. His work began to suffer too - he'd get so caught up in checking his surroundings that he couldn't focus on design tasks. Coworkers noticed his distraction and asked if everything was okay, but Kofi just shrugged it off as stress. The isolation took its toll on Kofi's relationships - friends stopped inviting him out when he kept declining, assuming he was flaking or not interested. His parents worried that something was wrong, but Kofi couldn't bear to tell them about the stalking, convinced they'd be disappointed in his inability to handle it himself. Lately, though, things had reached a breaking point. A new design project required him to collaborate with a team remotely - which meant opening up his laptop camera and screen-sharing for hours on end. Every time he saw his own face staring back at him, Kofi felt like he was inviting another predator into his life. His heart would start racing as he frantically scanned the room behind him, convinced someone was lurking just out of sight. That's when Kofi knew he needed help - not just to deal with the stalking itself, but with the toxic fears and self-blame that had taken hold. He'd finally reached a point where he realized he couldn't shake this alone - what frightened him most was losing himself completely in the darkness of his own mind.
